name: DashboardGrid
description: A dashboard the people using it can rearrange, and a model can write.

props.name: children
props.description: The widgets. Each `<Widget id>` is placed by the layout item of that id; one with no item is left to flow.

props.name: layout
props.description: Controlled layout. Leave it out and the grid owns it.

props.name: defaultLayout
props.description: What it starts as. The layout is normalized on the way in, so a generated one need not be tidy.

props.name: onLayoutChange
props.description: Fires on every cell a drag crosses and every arrow key, with the whole normalized layout.

props.name: onLayoutCommit
props.description: Fires once when the interaction ends — the place for the write a per-cell callback is too noisy for.

props.name: columns
props.description: How many columns, at one width or at several: `12`, or `{ xs: 1, md: 6, xxl: 12 }` — the default — which is one column until the dashboard is 28rem wide, six from there and twelve from 42rem. Each is a projection of the one layout, computed rather than measured, so the browser picks between classes; the smallest count is also what a container narrower than every size named here gets.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: The height of one row, on the ÷4 spacing scale. Default `24` — 6rem.

props.name: editable
props.description: Whether widgets can be moved and resized. The handles exist only in edit mode, and only where the layout's own columns are being rendered.

props.name: label
props.description: What the set of widgets is called. A list needs a name where a page holds more than one.

props.name: labelledBy
props.description: The same, naming an element that already says it.

keyboard.action: Picks a widget up from either handle, and drops it again.
One cell, along the reading axis: in a right-to-left page ArrowLeft moves a widget to the *right*. On the resize handle they add and remove a column or a row.
Puts the widget back where it was picked up from, and the layout with it.

a11y: The grid is a `role="list"` named by `label`, and each placed widget a `role="listitem"` — so a reader is told how many widgets there are and which one this is, which a set of `region` landmarks would drown out.

Moving and resizing are a **grab**: Enter or Space on a handle picks the widget up, the arrows move it, Enter drops it and Escape puts it back. Every step is announced in a polite live region that is there before there is anything to say.
The handles are real buttons with `aria-pressed` for the grabbed state and an `aria-describedby` naming the instructions, rather than an HTML5 drag, which no screen reader drives.
